slots.label: Heading 1
slots.default: What we account for in Leeds

slots.label: Paragraph 2
slots.default: Leeds has one of the largest concentrations of financial, legal and professional services outside London. That density changes the IT conversation, because a majority of the businesses we would support there operate inside somebody’s regulatory perimeter.

slots.label: Heading 2
slots.default: Regulated firms have to evidence, not just assert

slots.label: Paragraph 5
slots.default: A law firm answering to the SRA and a financial firm answering to the FCA both need to show how access is controlled, how records are retained and what happens during an incident. Documentation is part of the service in that context, not an optional extra.

slots.label: Heading 3
slots.default: Client money and client data raise the stakes on email

slots.label: Paragraph 8
slots.default: Payment redirection fraud targets exactly this mix of sectors, and it arrives by email rather than through the network. Authentication, impersonation protection and a firm rule about verifying bank details by telephone do more good here than additional perimeter spending.

slots.label: Heading 4
slots.default: City-centre growth means frequent moves and fit-outs

slots.label: Paragraph 11
slots.default: Firms in Leeds expand into adjacent floors and relocate more often than average. Planning the network and connectivity lead times early is what keeps a move from becoming a fortnight of tethered laptops.

slots.label: Heading 5
slots.default: Onsite attendance from the South East, planned in advance

slots.label: Paragraph 14
slots.default: Engineers travel from London and Stevenage, so a Leeds visit is scheduled work. Given how much of the city’s business base is desk-and-cloud rather than machinery, that matters less here than in a manufacturing town, and remote resolution covers the large majority of what arises.

slots.label: Heading 6
slots.default: A health and public-sector technology cluster

slots.label: Paragraph 17
slots.default: Leeds has an established concentration of health-related and public-sector digital organisations alongside its financial and legal core. Suppliers into that ecosystem are routinely asked to evidence security controls and data handling formally, which makes documentation part of the deliverable rather than an afterthought.

slots.label: Heading 7
slots.default: Retention is a records decision before it is a storage one

slots.label: Paragraph 20
slots.default: Regulated firms carry obligations about how long client records are kept and how they are produced if asked. That is a policy question, but it lands as a technology one: retention rules on mailboxes and document libraries, a legal hold that survives an employee leaving, and a search that can actually find everything on a matter. Setting it deliberately is straightforward. Reconstructing it later, from mailboxes people have tidied and archives nobody documented, is the expensive version.

slots.label: Heading 8
slots.default: Sending client documents by attachment is the habit worth breaking

slots.label: Paragraph 23
slots.default: The safest change most professional firms can make is to stop moving sensitive documents as email attachments. A portal or a secure share means access can be withdrawn, viewing is recorded, and a message sent to the wrong recipient does not hand over the file. It also removes the temptation to protect a document with a password sent in a second email, which is not protection at all if both messages reach the same inbox.
